before.title: Air Conditioning Failure — Refrigerant Hose Leak and Early Compressor Faults
before.description: A recurring complaint pattern on the Brazilian Kwid: the AC stops cooling because a refrigerant hose routed low near the engine kinks and develops a pinhole leak, slowly venting the gas — the system still appears to work (panel lights, blower runs) but blows warm or only slightly cool air. The hose leak is reported as especially common on 2018 models, and shops frequently misdiagnose it as a simple gas recharge, which fails again within weeks. There is also a cluster of Reclame Aqui complaints about compressors failing very early (one documented at just 20,000 km, cooling only at high RPM) and abnormal noise/vibration when the compressor engages.
before.solution: Have the system leak-tested with UV dye or an electronic sniffer before paying for repeat recharges — check the known trouble spot where the hose runs below/near the engine. Replace the leaking hose and recharge with the correct refrigerant quantity; if the compressor only cools at high RPM or is noisy, test compressor output pressure and replace the compressor if it is worn. On cars still in the 3-year factory warranty, insist on warranty coverage since early compressor failure is well documented.
symptoms: AC blows warm or only slightly cool air
AC only cools at high engine RPM
Noise or vibration when the compressor engages
Refrigerant recharge stops working within weeks
AC gradually loses cooling capacity over months

before.title: Brake Judder and Fade from Undersized Solid Front Discs (Pre-Facelift)
before.description: Pre-facelift Kwids used small 215 mm solid (non-ventilated) front brake discs that overheat under sustained or hard use, leading to fade on long descents and disc warping that owners feel as violent pedal pulsation and steering wheel vibration when braking — often accompanied by metallic noise even with new pads. The trade magazine O Mecânico documents that Renault replaced the solid discs with larger 238 mm ventilated discs in the 2019/2020 line update specifically to improve sustained-braking efficiency and reduce fading; the solid- and ventilated-disc parts (including pads) are not interchangeable. Brake judder remains one of the most commonly cited chronic complaints on early cars in Brazilian owner-problem roundups.
before.solution: On pre-facelift cars with pedal pulsation, replace (not machine) the warped front discs and pads as an axle set — aftermarket ventilated-disc kits for the facelift hub are sold in Brazil, but the straightforward fix is new quality solid discs and pads matched to the original 215 mm spec. Use engine braking on long descents to limit heat buildup. If vibration persists after new discs, have hub runout and wheel bearing seating checked, as improper mounting also causes judder.
symptoms: Brake pedal pulsates or shudders when stopping
Steering wheel vibrates during braking
Metallic grinding noise even with new pads
Brakes fade on long downhill stretches
Burning smell from the front wheels after hard braking

before.title: Heavy, Squeaky Clutch and Reverse-Gear Grinding
before.description: The Kwid's cable-operated clutch is a chronic complaint across all model years in Brazil: the pedal becomes heavy and stiff, creaks loudly when pressed (owners compare it to an old door hinge or a trumpet sound when reversing), and reverse gear grinds or refuses to engage. Documented causes are the clutch cable losing lubrication and binding, the release fork deforming, and pressure-plate diaphragm springs weakening — several owners report symptoms starting under 5,000 km, and the local press (Diarinho) covered a case where a dealership dismissed the noise as 'normal.' Vrum additionally documents a smaller number of more severe gearbox failures where first, second, or reverse stop engaging entirely, some within months of purchase.
before.solution: Lubricating the old clutch cable quiets the squeak only for a few days — the documented lasting fix is replacing the clutch kit (disc, pressure plate, release bearing) together with a new clutch cable and checking the release fork for deformation. For hard reverse engagement, fully depress the clutch and pause briefly (or pass through a forward gear first) per Renault's own quick guide; persistent grinding after a new clutch indicates the cable/fork repair was incomplete. Total gearbox failures on cars in warranty should be replaced by Renault under warranty.
symptoms: Heavy or stiff clutch pedal
Loud squeak or creak when pressing the clutch
Grinding noise when engaging reverse
Difficulty engaging reverse or first gear
Trumpet-like noise while reversing

before.title: Launch-Era Recall: Brake Component Cracks and Fuel Line Perforation
before.description: In November 2017 Renault do Brasil recalled 21,802 Kwids built between March 1, 2016 and November 2, 2017 (chassis HJ524902 to JJ999218) for two defects announced together. First, brake system components could develop cracks, potentially causing braking inefficiency or wheel lock-up with loss of directional control. Second, the fuel supply tube was routed/positioned incorrectly and could chafe and perforate, leaking fuel into the engine compartment with fire risk. A related recall in January 2018 covered a batch of September 2017-production cars whose engine cradle (subframe) welds could rupture due to a supplier defect. All campaigns are listed on Renault Brazil's official recall page.
before.solution: Check the chassis number against the recall (Renault Brazil recall portal or 0800 055 5615) and have the recall service performed free of charge at a Renault dealer: inspection and replacement of brake components (up to 1 day) and inspection/repositioning or replacement of the fuel tube (about 1 hour). On any used 2017-2018 Kwid purchase, confirm recall completion — open recalls are still performed at no cost.
symptoms: Soft or sinking brake pedal
Reduced braking efficiency
Wheel lock-up under braking
Fuel smell from the engine bay
Visible fuel leak under the hood

before.title: Rear Axle Support Cracking — 2025 Safety Recall (2021-2023 Production)
before.description: In June 2025 Renault do Brasil recalled Kwids manufactured between May 5, 2021 and June 12, 2023 (chassis J000006 to J986154) because the rear axle support can be impacted under specific road conditions and develop cracks (fissures), altering the vehicle's original driving characteristics. In extreme cases the support can fracture, increasing the risk of an accident with injury to occupants and third parties. Brazilian press (Terra, Metrópoles, Autos Segredos) reported the campaign, which also covered some Duster units, and noted it followed an in-depth investigation with local testing — a finding consistent with long-running owner complaints about the rear suspension's fragility on rough Brazilian roads.
before.solution: Check the chassis number on Renault Brazil's recall portal (www.renault.com.br) or call 0800 055 5615 and schedule the free recall service, which began June 5, 2025. The dealer inspects the rear axle support and replaces components as needed; the service takes from 30 minutes up to 8 hours depending on whether replacement is required. Until the recall is performed, have the rear axle mounting points inspected if you hear knocking from the rear or notice handling changes.
symptoms: Knocking or creaking from the rear suspension over bumps
Rear of the vehicle feels unstable or wanders
Visible cracks at the rear axle mounting points
Uneven rear tire wear
Noticeable change in handling or ride behavior

before.title: Steering Column Support Bracket Breakage
before.description: One of the most serious and widely reported chronic defects on early Brazilian-market Kwids. The bracket that supports the electric power steering column can crack and break during normal driving, in extreme cases letting the steering wheel drop into the driver's lap with loss of vehicle control. Brazilian outlets (Vrum, Grupo Sentinela, Mundo do Automóvel) document numerous owner reports, concentrated on cars built through 2019, and note that despite the volume of complaints Renault never issued a recall. Dealer quotes reported by owners ranged from roughly R$3,000 to R$5,800 for a complete electric steering column assembly replacement, and several owners only obtained goodwill repairs after escalating publicly.
before.solution: Have the steering column support inspected immediately at any sign of play, clunking, or noise from the column — this is a drive-safety item. The fix is replacement of the column support or, in most documented cases, the complete electric power steering column assembly. Owners of 2017-2019 cars have had partial success obtaining goodwill (cortesia) coverage from Renault Brazil even outside warranty by registering complaints through Renault customer service and Procon/Reclame Aqui; document the defect with photos before repair.
symptoms: Clunking or knocking noise from the steering column
Excessive play or looseness in the steering wheel
Steering wheel suddenly drops toward the driver's lap
Metal fragments falling into the driver's footwell
Loss of steering control while driving
